title: Rust tunnel_auth evicts replay/revocation floors under capacity pressure; Python fail-closes with CAPACITY (P-R divergence)
description: Found by 3x codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-0rep (two reviewers converged, P1/P2 family). rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs floors are bounded at N with silent LRU eviction: accept_post floor_index fallback :339-348 evicts min-used floor, revoke() :247-256 does the same on unknown-key revoke with full floors (returns Ok). A revoked floor's used is never refreshed after revoke() (its entry was deleted; authorize_decapsulation refresh :408-414 only touches floors matching an ACCEPTED claim), so a revoked floor is always the first eviction candidate. If evicted, replaying the captured revoked POST (claim still unexpired) finds no floor and no entry -> accept_post re-accepts it and re-arms the data plane. Python mirror python/src/lichen/gateway/tunnel_auth.py never evicts floors: floors capped at _max_history (4x max_entries, :388), receive_post denies CAPACITY when full (:484-485), revoke() raises 'authorization replay history is full' and mutates nothing (:503-505); _revoked persists until genuine re-arm (:491) or root change (:435). Same inputs: Rust accepts, Python denies. Exploitability is low (forcing eviction of the target key needs N distinct newly-accepted keys, which requires fresh root-signed grants, not replays) but it is a semantic weakening plus a hard cross-impl divergence. Fix: mirror Python - give floors their own bounded history that fail-closes with a Capacity/TunnelAuthError variant when full (accept_post and revoke), never silently evict; align capacity constant with Python's 4x; add unit tests for accept-on-full and revoke-on-full; add shared vector post_cases if the corpus schema can express capacity denials.
close_reason: Fixed: tunnel_auth replay floors are no longer silently LRU-evicted. (1) replay_floors is now [[Option<ReplayFloor>; 4]; N] (FLOOR_SLOTS_PER_ENTRY=4, mirroring Python _max_history = 4 * max_entries; stable-Rust nested array since N*4 const arithmetic is unsupported); (2) accept_post of a NEW key with no free floor slot returns Err(TunnelAuthError::Capacity) instead of evicting the min-used floor - the old behavior let an attacker whose 5th grant evicted a REVOKED floor replay the captured revoked POST and re-arm the data plane; (3) revoke of an unknown key on a full history returns Err(Capacity) (Python raises 'authorization replay history is full') and, per review, now resolves the slot BEFORE any mutation so a refused revoke leaves the table untouched (struct invariant 'validation before mutation' restored); (4) existing keys reusing their own floor slot are never capacity-gated (Python parity); (5) Capacity maps through the uniform COAP_FORBIDDEN_CODE fail-closed policy; (6) struct doc updated. New test floor_capacity_fails_closed_and_retains_revoked_floor pins: 4 distinct keys fill the history, 5th accept -> Capacity, revoke-on-full -> Capacity, replay of the REVOKED A's captured post -> Revoked (the exploit pin), existing-key floor advance still accepted. Shared vector rows NOT added: the tunnel_authorization corpus schema expresses single-post cases only and cannot encode the table-full precondition; also generator drift on that file is tracked by wtxl (macOS canonical regeneration required) - noted rather than forced. Verification on heft: gateway lib 222/222 (new test + all prior), clippy clean, fmt applied. 3x delegated codereview: correctness found revoke-premutation (fixed) + stale doc (fixed); security PASS (capacity check order after auth/expiry/replay - no occupancy oracle for unauthenticated peers; fill-by-valid-grants is Python-parity, not divergence); edge PASS (N=0, equal-path_seq, flattened index boundaries exact, capacity boundary genuine with no mutation on refusal).
